summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for an acute flare of chronic back and bilateral sacroiliac joint pain, worse on the left, with difficulty ambulating. He recently completed a prednisone taper but declined further steroids or biologics due to recurrent infections. Labs showed no active infection or inflammation. Pain was managed with Dilaudid and cyclobenzaprine, and a new prescription for nortriptyline was started for chronic pain. He was discharged home in stable condition after two days with instructions to follow up with rheumatology, pain management, and his PCP, continue home medications, and wean off opioids as able.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
